NTSB Releases Preliminary Findings on Amazon Plane Crash

The National Transportation Safety Board (NTSB) has shared initial findings from the cockpit voice and flight data recorder of the fatal Amazon “Prime Air” crash in Miami. The crash resulted in five fatalities and five injuries. The NTSB revealed that a pilot had warned that the aircraft was “too fast” before the crash. The report did not specify which pilot issued the warnings.
Ford Faces Criticism Over China Ties
President Donald Trump’s Transportation Secretary, Sean Duffy, has criticized
Ford Motor Co

for its collaborations with several China-linked companies, citing potential U.S. security risks. Duffy expressed “profound concern” about Ford’s battery and vehicle-related arrangements with Chinese firms like CATL,
Geely Automobile Holdings Ltd.
and
BYD Co. Ltd

children: Elon Musk Refutes Autopilot Involvement in Fatal Crash
Tesla Inc.

CEO Elon Musk has denied that the company’s driver-assistance technology was involved in a fatal New York City crash. Musk argued that the crash would not have occurred if Autopilot had been in use. The crash involved a Tesla Model Y crashing into scaffolding, resulting in one fatality.
Tesla’s Cybercab Could Undercut Waymo

According to Goldman Sachs, Tesla could operate its Cybercab for up to 30 cents per mile less than rival autonomous vehicles if it achieves its targeted production costs. Goldman analysts estimated that Tesla’s low-cost vehicle design and camera-only sensor system could strengthen its robotaxi economics.
Ford Responds to Criticism Over China Ties

Ford Motor Company’s stock traded higher after the automaker refuted criticism from Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy over its ties to China. Ford stated that Duffy’s letter contained factual errors about its BlueOval Battery Park Michigan and its agreement with China’s CATL.
